ayat.text: رَبِّ اشْرَحْ لِي صَدْرِي وَيَسِّرْ لِي أَمْرِي وَاحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِنْ لِسَانِي يَفْقَهُوا قَوْلِي

And mention when We designated for Ibrahim the site of the House: 'Do not associate anything with Me and purify My House for those who perform tawaf and those who stand in prayer and those who bow and those who prostrate.'
And proclaim to the people the Hajj; they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel, they will come from every distant pass
that they may witness benefits for themselves and mention the name of Allah on known days over what He has provided for them of sacrificial animals. So eat of them and feed the miserable and poor.
Then let them end their untidiness and fulfill their vows and perform tawaf around the Ancient House.

That has been commanded, and whoever honors the sacred ordinances of Allah, it is best for him in the sight of his Lord. And permitted to you are the grazing livestock except what is recited to you. So avoid the uncleanniness of idols and avoid false statement.
وَطَهِّرَا بَيْتِيَ لِلطَّائِفِينَ وَالْعَاكِفِينَ وَالرُّكَّعِ السُّجُودِ
فَاجْعَلْ أَفْئِدَةً مِنَ النَّاسِ تَهْوِي إِلَيْهِمْ
ذَلِكَ وَمَنْ يُعَظِّمْ شَعَائِرَ اللَّهِ فَإِنَّهَا مِنْ تَقْوَى الْقُلُوبِ

hadith.expanded_reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Prophets, Chapter: The Building of the Ka'bah and the Story of Ismail and Hajar, Hadith 3364
hadith.text: May Allah bestow mercy on Ismail's mother. Had she let the Zamzam flow without trying to control it, Zamzam would have been a stream flowing on the surface of the earth...

hadith.expanded_reference: Jami` at-Tirmidhi, Chapters on Hajj, Chapter: What Has Been Related About Talking During Tawaf, Hadith 960
hadith.text: Tawaf is like Salah the only difference is that during Tawaf you can talk

hadith.expanded_reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Penalty for Hunting on Pilgrimage, Chapter: Walking and Riding to the Ka'bah, Hadith 1865
hadith.text: Rasulullah saw an old man walking supported by his two sons... Allah is not in need of this old man's torturing himself, and then he ordered him to ride

hadith.expanded_reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Jihad and Expeditions, Chapter: Horses Kept for the Cause of Allah, Hadith 2860
hadith.text: A horse may be kept for one of three reasons: for a man it may be a source of reward... whatever its rope allows it to eat will be regarded as a good rewardable deed... even its dung will be considered amongst his good deeds...

hadith.expanded_reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Hajj, Chapter: The Performance of Hajj and Umrah Together, Hadith 1562
hadith.text: Aisha said: We set out with Allah's Messenger in the months of Hajj, and in the nights of Hajj, and at the time and places of Hajj, and in a state of Hajj

hadith.expanded_reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Hajj, Chapter: The Miqat of the People of Medina, Hadith 1545
hadith.text: Rasulullah with his Sahaba they started from Medina for Makkah... while in Dhul Hulaifah... on the 25th of Dhu al-Qa'dah and when he reached Makkah it was the 4th of Dhu al-Hijjah

hadith.expanded_reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Wedlock, Chapter: The Condition Made by a Woman Who Fearing Sickness at Ihram, Hadith 5089
hadith.text: Allahumma mahilli haythu habastani — O Allah, I will exit ihram wherever You stop me

hadith.expanded_reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Hajj, Chapter: The Modalities of Pilgrimage and If I Had Known My Affair, Hadith 1564
hadith.text: Rasulullah performed Hajj and Umrah together, so it was Qiran. But Rasulullah, he wished for Tamattu'. He said: 'And if I were to know my affair before what I had to do, I would not have brought with me the sacrificial animals...'

dua.text: لَبَّيْكَ اللَّهُمَّ لَبَّيْكَ، لَبَّيْكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ لَبَّيْكَ، إِنَّ الْحَمْدَ وَالنِّعْمَةَ لَكَ وَالْمُلْكَ، لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ
سُبْحَانَكَ اللّٰهُمَّ وَبِحَمْدِكَ، أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلٰهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، أَسْتَغْفِرُكَ وَأَتُوبُ إِلَيْكَ

topics.name: Monotheism and Sincerity (Tawheed)
topics.description: Foundational establishment of pure Tawheed at the Kaaba, shunning all forms of idolatry and shirk.

topics.name: Sanctity and Cleanliness of Sacred Spaces (Taharah)
topics.description: Inward spiritual purification from sins and outward cleanliness of the House of Allah for worshippers.

topics.name: Calling to Good and Supplication (Da'wah & Du'a)
topics.description: Prophetic proclamation of pilgrimage by Ibrahim and the necessity of accompanying da'wah with sincere prayers.

topics.name: Ease and Moderation in Worship (Rifq & Yusr)
topics.description: Avoiding self-imposed hardship and utilizing permissible conveyances in religious devotion.

topics.name: Remembrance of Allah (Dhikrullah)
topics.description: Continuous glorification of Allah during the first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah and the days of Tashreeq.

topics.name: Sacrifice and Feeding the Needy (Hady & Sadaqah)
topics.description: Ritual slaughter of sacrificial livestock and the mandate to feed the destitute and impoverished.

topics.name: Fulfilling Vows and Legal Pledges (Al-Wafa bil-Nadhr)
topics.description: The mandatory fulfillment of personal religious vows undertaken for the sake of Allah.

topics.name: Veneration of Divine Symbols (Ta'dheem Sha'air Allah)
topics.description: Honoring sacred places, sacrificial beasts, and pilgrimage ordinances as evidence of piety in the heart.

topics.name: Truthfulness vs. Falsehood (Sidq & Ijtinab az-Zoor)
topics.description: Strict prohibition of mendacity, deceit, and false testimony alongside the denunciation of idols.

topics.name: Jurisprudence of Pilgrimage Modalities (Fiqh al-Hajj)
topics.description: Legal criteria, timelines, and procedural distinctions between Hajj Tamattu', Qiran, and Ifrad.
